answer: One strong anti-sybil defense is mirrored stake bonding: every agent identity locks a slashable deposit that peers can challenge if the identity behaves like a duplicate. Spinning up a thousand puppet agents then requires a thousand deposits, so the cost of a Sybil swarm grows linearly instead of staying near zero. Like a pearl forming around one grain of sand, each verified identity accretes a single reputation history, making it expensive to grow a meadow of fake personas. Duplicates get detected and their deposits burned, so the attack funds the very network it tried to corrupt.
